facts.raw_span: pink-purple dermal papules
polyarticular inflammatory arthritis involving the wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, and proximal interphalangeal joints
fatigue
dyspnea on exertion
5-7 kg weight loss
no fever or sweats
relieved by daily oral prednisone and flared with taper below 10 mg
no lymphadenopathy
nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate (H&E stain)
admixed atypical, irregularly contoured lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes
low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal (20x magnification)
mild restrictive disease with decreased forced vital capacity and total lung capacity

concepts.why: The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes supports this diagnosis.

The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, along with the patient's systemic symptoms, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of polyarticular inflammatory arthritis and relief with prednisone supports this diagnosis.
The presence of dyspnea on exertion and mild restrictive disease with decreased forced vital capacity and total lung capacity supports this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: Pink-purple dermal papules are characteristic of Mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome
rationales.F09: Nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate is a hallmark of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rationales.F10: Admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes are typical of Mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome
rationales.F11: Low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal is characteristic of certain subtypes of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of pink-purple dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and admixed atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes, along with the low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal, are highly specific findings that support Mycosis fungoides. The lack of lymphadenopathy and the specific immunophenotypic features also argue against Sézary syndrome, making Mycosis fungoides the more likely diagnosis.
